title: November Examination: Paper 2
instructions: This paper consists of SIX questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Clearly show ALL calculations. Give reasons for all statements in geometry.
You may use an approved scientific calculator unless stated otherwise.
Round off answers to TWO decimal places, unless stated otherwise. Diagrams are not necessarily drawn to scale.

context.caption: Temperature at noon and number of cold drinks sold at a tuck shop

questions.prompt: Determine the equation of the least-squares regression line.
Write down the correlation coefficient and describe the correlation.
Predict the number of drinks sold when the temperature is 25 °C.
Would it be reasonable to use the line to predict sales at 5 °C? Explain.
questions.memo:
✓ No (1)
✓ 5 °C is far outside the data range (extrapolation); the prediction is negative and meaningless (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between interpolation and extrapolation, and calculate the average number of cold drinks sold per day over the six days.
questions.memo:
✓ Interpolation: predicting within the range of the data (1)
✓ Extrapolation: predicting outside the range (1)
✓ Interpolation is more reliable (1)
✓ Total $= 238$ (1)
✓ Mean $\approx 39{,}67$ drinks (1)

context.text: The circle with equation $x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0$ has centre M. $P(5; 1)$ is a point on the circle.

questions.prompt: Determine the coordinates of M and the radius of the circle.
Determine the equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
Does the point $Q(6; -6)$ lie inside, on or outside the circle? Show working.
Find the length of PQ in simplest surd form.
Determine the equation of the circle that has PQ as a diameter.
Without a calculator, show that $\sin 105^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}$.
If $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ and $\theta$ is acute, find $\cos 2\theta$ without a calculator.
Prove the identity: $\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x + 1} = \tan x$
questions.memo:
✓ $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$ (1)
✓ $\cos 2x + 1 = 2\cos^2 x$ (1)
✓ $\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x}$ (1)
✓ $= \tan x$ (1)

questions.prompt: Determine the general solution of $\cos 2x - 3\sin x - 2 = 0$.
Simplify without a calculator: $\dfrac{\sin 2x \cdot \cos(90^\circ - x)}{1 - \cos 2x}$
questions.memo:
✓ $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$ (1)
✓ $\cos(90^\circ - x) = \sin x$ (1)
✓ $1 - \cos 2x = 2\sin^2 x$ (1)
✓ $\frac{2\sin^2 x\cos x}{2\sin^2 x} = \cos x$ (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Trigonometry in two and three dimensions

context.text: A and B are two points on level ground, 150 m apart. F is the foot of a vertical tower FT. $\hat{FAB} = 48^\circ$ and $\hat{FBA} = 72^\circ$. The angle of elevation of T from B is $18^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Calculate BF, correct to two decimal places.
Calculate the height of the tower FT, correct to two decimal places.
Calculate the area of △ABF, correct to two decimal places.
Show that, in general, if $AB = d$, $\hat{FAB} = \alpha$, $\hat{FBA} = \beta$ and the angle of elevation of T from B is $\theta$, then $FT = \dfrac{d\sin\alpha\tan\theta}{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}$.
In △PQR, ST ∥ QR with S on PQ and T on PR. PS = 6 cm, SQ = 9 cm and TR = 12 cm. Calculate PT, giving a reason.
In △ABC, $\hat{BAC} = 90^\circ$ and AD ⊥ BC with D on BC. (a) Prove that △ABD ||| △CBA. (b) Hence, if BD = 4 cm and DC = 12 cm, calculate AB.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ $\hat{B}$ common (1) ✓ $\hat{ADB} = \hat{BAC} = 90^\circ$ (1) ✓ △ABD ||| △CBA (∠∠∠) (1)
(b) ✓ $\frac{AB}{CB} = \frac{BD}{BA}$, so $AB^2 = BD \cdot BC$ (1) ✓ $AB^2 = 4 \times 16 = 64$ (1) ✓ AB = 8 cm (1)

questions.prompt: O is the centre of the circle and A, B, C and D are on the circle. $\hat{AOC} = 130^\circ$ with B on the major arc and D on the minor arc. TA is a tangent at A and $\hat{TAD} = 40^\circ$. Calculate, with reasons: (a) $\hat{ABC}$ (b) $\hat{ADC}$ (c) $\hat{ABD}$
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ $\hat{ABC} = 65^\circ$ (∠ at centre = 2 × ∠ at circumference) (2)
(b) ✓ $\hat{ADC} = 115^\circ$ (opp ∠s of cyclic quad) (1)
(c) ✓ $\hat{ABD} = 40^\circ$ (tan chord theorem) (2)

questions.prompt: In △ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC such that DE ∥ BC. AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm. (a) Prove that △ADE ||| △ABC. (b) Calculate BC.
Calculate the mean and the (population) standard deviation of: $12; 15; 18; 20; 25$.
The ages of a group are summarised by: minimum 14, $Q_1$ = 16, median 17, $Q_3$ = 22, maximum 30. Describe the skewness of the data and identify whether 30 is an outlier.
questions.memo:
✓ The median is closer to $Q_1$, so the data is positively skewed (2)
✓ Upper fence $= 22 + 1{,}5(6) = 31$ (1)
✓ 30 is not an outlier (1)

questions.prompt: In Question 1, the correlation coefficient is about $0{,}998$. Explain in words what this tells the tuck-shop owner.
questions.memo:
✓ There is a very strong positive linear relationship (1)
✓ Hotter days are associated with more cold drinks sold (1)
✓ The regression line can be used for reliable predictions within the data range (1)

questions.prompt: A spherical ball has a diameter of 22 cm. (a) Calculate its volume. (b) The ball is packed into the smallest possible cube-shaped box. What percentage of the box is empty space?
